Best mattress in a box Australia 2026: 8 to consider for a good night’s sleep

Looking for the best mattress in a box in Australia? We've rounded up our favourites, with options for cooling, adjustable, supportive mattresses and affordable foam designs
WriterDanielle Grover
WriterJanet Guan
21 September, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article

While the days of heading to a mattress store to systematically lie on every bed may be past us, so too are the days taking a gamble on a random mattress to be delivered to your door. Mattress in a box retailers have come a long way in the last ten years, with multitudes of options available, including foam, latex, and hybrid mattresses with adjustable firmness, temperature regulation, and movement isolation. Plus, most of the better ones offer an extended trial period as standard, so you can try the mattress in your home, commitment-free and if it’s not a match send it back.

Advertisement

The mattress in a box concept – where the mattress itself is compressed and rolled into a manoeuvrable, easy to deliver box – provides a convenient and affordable way to get a comfortable mattress delivered to your door. Given we spend approximately one third of our lives in bed, it’s definitely crucial to invest the time in finding the right mattress for you to ensure you have a good night’s sleep. Boxed mattresses have quickly become one of the most popular ways to upgrade your quality of sleep. The catch? Not all are created equal.

Here’s our guide to selecting the best mattress in a box for you – whether you’re a side-sleeper, a couple, or you run hot, plus our top picks based on brand reliability and comfort.

What to look for when choosing a mattress in a box

Mattresses come in a variety of shapes and sizes, and having the right one can be truly life changing. “When choosing the best mattress you should consider features that are going to support a deeper, more restful sleep,” says Dr. Verena Senn, Head of Sleep Research at Emma Sleep.

If you’re looking to buy a new mattress in a box, there are a few important considerations – from memory foam mattresses to hybrid mattresses – so finding one that offers the optimal support for a good night’s sleep, while still being able to be rolled up and delivered in a box, is vital.

According to the product design team at Koala, when selecting the right mattress it’s important to firstly identify the quality of materials used. The main materials used in mattresses in a box are foam, memory foam, latex, pocket springs or a combination of all, however, there are many different types of these materials. “A mattress in a box should have a high quality foam in the comfort layers, and a base that provides support to the sleeper,” explains the Koala team.

Next, you need to consider the customer service and returns policy of the mattress brand. “The body may need a few days to several weeks to get used to a new mattress and therefore should be tested over a longer period,” explains Dr. Verena Senn.

“Trialling products in-store is a good start, but you usually do not test the mattress there in the same positions you actually sleep in.” Testing it over many nights in your everyday life is, therefore, more crucial to making an informed decision.

Advertisement

Finally, you need to be familiar with what style of sleeper you are based on your preferred sleeping positions. This will allow you to identify the best mattress to suit your needs. The experts at Choice identify three types of mattress firmness:

Firm mattress: For stomach sleepers, a firmer mattress will help ensure your spine is kept properly aligned.
Medium firm mattress: Ideal for those who sleep on their back as it will offer support for the spine, back and neck while keeping you comfortable.
Soft mattress: Ideal for those who sleep on their side as it will offer support and pressure relief for the hips and shoulders.

“Depending on body size or weight, the firmness of a mattress can also determine whether you lie in an ergonomically correct position, as this influences how much you sink in,” says Dr. Verena Senn.

How long will a boxed mattress last?

With proper care, a good quality box mattress should last just as long as a traditional mattress. The Koala product design team suggests replacing your mattress every 10 years for hygiene reasons.

Is memory foam or pocket spring better?

This will depend on what type of sleeper you are, or what sleeping position you prefer. For side sleepers, a memory foam mattress is much better at contouring to your body in comparison. However, if you sleep on your back, both pocket spring or memory foam are great options.

Furthermore, if you’re sharing a bed, memory foam is best at minimising partner disturbance due to its ability to isolate movement better.

Advertisement

Can you sleep on a mattress in a box right away?

As boxed mattresses are packaged tightly, it does mean you’ll need to give it some time to expand when you unroll it for the first time. This can take anywhere between a few hours to 48 hours, depending on the brand you choose.

How will my mattress be delivered?

Some mattress brands offer free delivery along with purchase and even same-day delivery. The mattress generally comes vacuum sealed inside the box and expand when you piece the plastic.
